title: Dedicated Capacity: Bandwidth Reservoir Pricing and Security Questionnaire Template
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Enterprise customers want predictable throughput guarantees for heavy inference workloads but also demand contractual simplicity and a fast security questionnaire (SQ) turnaround. Current 'commit + burst' bundles complicate procurement and often trigger long SQ cycles when we recommend multiple burst credit variants. Goal: Propose a new pricing/packaging model — 'Bandwidth Reservoir' — that (1) simplifies contract language, (2) provides deterministic monthly capacity with short-term smoothing for spikes, and (3) maps cleanly to the enterprise SQ responses (networking, KMS, audit logging). Deliver a pricing experiment matrix, rollout plan for pilots, and a draft enterprise SQ template aligned with legal and security screening requirements.
background_and_rationale: We observed recurring objections in enterprise pilot negotiations: (1) too many moving parts in burst credit calculations, (2) opaque effective costs during sustained spikes, and (3) security questionnaire answers that require cross-team sign-off because product packaging doesn't clearly state data residency, key management, and audit retention. The 'Bandwidth Reservoir' frames capacity as a reservoir (base committed throughput) plus a managed smoothing window (tokens that draw down briefly to absorb spikes). This is conceptually simpler for procurement (one SLA, one baseline price band) and easier for security to document: reservoir = committed capacity; smoothing window = transient buffer handled by platform policy and audit logs.
goals: Create 3 starter pricing bands (Small, Medium, Large) expressed as $/GPU-hour baseline + reservoir tokens/month
Produce an A/B pilot plan comparing 'Bandwidth Reservoir' vs existing reserve+burst offering with 10 pilot customers
Deliver a one-page SQ template mapping each pricing element to security controls (KMS, SOC2, VPC peering, audit logs)
Define acceptance metrics for pilot (cost predictability, p95 latency, time-to-SQ completion)
Prepare contract language snippets and implementation checklist for sales and solutions engineers
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Simplicity vs optimal unit economics: single-reservoir bands may slightly increase tail cost for very bursty customers compared to finely tuned burst credits
Legal clarity vs flexibility: fixed reservoirs reduce negotiation flexibility for bespoke enterprise deals
Operational burden: requires dashboarding to show reservoir utilization and automated notifications when smoothing windows approach depletion
proposed_pricing_models: Model A — Reservoir Bands (recommended pilot): Base price per reserved GPU-hour + monthly reservoir tokens (1 token = 1 GPU-minute at burst rate). Example: Small: $0.42/GPU-hour + 45k tokens/month; Medium: $0.38/GPU-hour + 180k tokens/month; Large: $0.34/GPU-hour + 600k tokens/month

Model B — Tiered Consumption (alternative): Fixed monthly commit with dynamic overage at a predictable surcharge (e.g., +35% per-token beyond commit), priced for customers who prefer simple overage pricing
Model C — Time-windowed Credits (experimental): Allocate credits that renew daily with carryover cap — useful for workloads with predictable diurnal patterns but more complex for contracts
experiment_plan: Select 8-12 pilot customers across SMB and mid-market with varied burstiness profiles
Run a 90-day side-by-side pricing comparison; instrument telemetry to collect cost per effective token and p95 latency under burst events
Contract terms: 90-day opt-in pilot with credit offsets to neutralize first-month bill impact
Success criteria: median cost variance <= 10% vs existing product for non-bursty customers; >25% reduction in legal/SQ turnaround time; dashboards show reservoir utilization and <5% surprise overages
acceptance_criteria: Pricing bands published in pricing repo and visible in Console pricing simulator
SQ template signed off by Security and Legal with mapped control IDs
Pilot cohort onboarded and telemetry dashboards validating reservoir math
Sales enablement one-pager and contract clause snippets available to AE and SE teams
risks: Customers with extremely bursty, unpredictable workloads may perceive higher costs; need clear calculator and time-bound pilot credits
Implementation complexity around accurate token accounting and UI exposition could delay GA
SQ mapping may uncover gaps (e.g., KMS key residency) that require platform changes or constrained packaging
